newsitem.title: JAPAN: US, Japan still far apart in air talks--US official.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan still far apart in air talks--US official.

text.p: The United States and Japan are still far apart in bilateral aviation negotiations after the first three days of formal talks in Tokyo, U.S. Assistant State Secretary Alan Larson told a news conference on Wednesday.
Larson said the next formal talks had been set for August 27-29 in Washington, when both sides would make efforts to reach an agreement by a September 30 deadline.
"The two sides are still far apart. Nonetheless, both sides agreed we should continue working towards the September target day for reaching an agreement," he said.
The two nations on Wednesday finished three days of talks aimed at forging an interim air pact. Last month they agreed to strike a new deal by the end of September.

The United States has called on Japan to agree that any interim deal will eventually lead to open skies, the U.S.-led policy of a free market without government restrictions for international air services.

"The Japanese delegation did not accept the open skies, but rather advocated what it called a fully liberalised market. The Japanese concept at this time is far removed from our views on full liberalisation," Larson said.
He said that the United States will continue to advocate a transition to open skies, which has already been agreed to by more than 20 nations.
Japan has sworn that it will never accept an open skies policy, however, arguing that it would lead to alliances dominated by U.S. carriers.
"The U.S. will make every effort to find a satisfactory resolution and one that is consistent with interests of both countries," Larson said.
